findings: F1 CRITICAL: Neither entry point runs. README/docstring command `python scripts/pipeline.py` does not exist (exit 2); actual `scripts/scripts/pipeline.py` fails with FileNotFoundError because ROOT (pipeline.py:45-48) resolves to <repo>/scripts, making DATA=<repo>/scripts/data/compounds.csv. No third party can reproduce anything from the README.

F2 HIGH: Active ACT-18 silently dropped — RDKit 2023.09.6 cannot kekulize it and the loader's bare `continue` (pipeline.py:53-66) discards it with no ID, reason, count check, or nonzero exit; 20 labelled actives become 19 used.

F3 HIGH: No input validation. `else: decoys.append(smi)` (line 64-65) classifies any non-exact-'1' label as a decoy: 'active', '1 ' (trailing space), '2', and a missing label all become negatives; empty SMILES is accepted as a valid active; missing smiles value raises AttributeError and missing column raises KeyError; duplicates and label conflicts are unflagged (11 fixtures recorded).

F4 CRITICAL: Evaluation folds are not independent. 26 unique decoys are replicated x20 into 520 rows (line 173-174), so 539 rows come from 45 distinct molecules; measured with the script's own StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle, seed 42), all 104 held-out decoy rows in every one of the 5 folds have an identical structure in that fold's training set. AUC=1.000 and EF1%=28.4 are arithmetic consequences of padding (max EF1% = 539/19 = 28.4; on 45 distinct molecules it would be 2.37), and EF1% is computed from a 5-row window.

F5 HIGH: The 'leave-scaffold-out' split is positional index arithmetic (lines 270-271), not a series lookup, despite compounds.csv carrying a `series` column. Because ACT-18 was dropped, the training block includes ACT-19 (ibrutinib series) and the test set is ACT-20 alone — a one-compound generalization test whose sensitivities can only be 0 or 1.

F6 HIGH: BEDROC implementation is numerically wrong (lines 114-126) — the exponential sum is never divided by the RIE normalization denominator. Versus RDKit CalcBEDROC: perfect ranking 0.00313 vs 1.0; all-active 0.0 vs 1.0; perfect ranking at n=540 0.00182 vs 1.0. Every reported BEDROC value is meaningless and inverted in the degenerate case.

F7 MEDIUM: Import-time side effects measured against a pristine copy — importing the module creates scripts/results/, switches the Matplotlib backend svg->agg, reseeds the process-wide NumPy RNG to 42, disables RDKit rdApp.warning, and applies a blanket warnings.filterwarnings('ignore') that swallowed a post-import UserWarning sentinel.

F8 CRITICAL (provenance): Candidate scores do not reproduce. The pipeline never writes final_hits.csv (one read, two plt.savefig writes in the whole file); reruns give NC5-01 TWCS 0.512 vs committed 0.82, NC5-04 0.067 vs 0.52, and the top rank changes from NC5-01 to NC5-02. Two different consensus definitions coexist (min-max-normalized at lines 217-220 vs raw mean at line 311). NC5-02 is structurally identical to training active ACT-19 (max Tanimoto 1.000). Four HBA values in final_hits.csv disagree with the repo's own compute_props (NC5-01 7 vs 10, NC5-04 7 vs 8, NC5-08 4 vs 5, NC5-10 6 vs 7). Committed ad_tier labels do not follow the manuscript's stated thresholds when recomputed (NC5-02, NC5-04, NC5-06).

F9 HIGH: Permutation significance is invalid. Code runs 5 permutations (line 236) and reports p via a raw fraction (line 251), printing p=0.000; scikit-learn documents the (C+1)/(n+1) estimator with best attainable p = 1/(n+1), i.e. 0.167 at n=5 and 0.032 even at the manuscript's n=30 — neither supports p<0.001. The null is also built on the duplicated matrix, so it inherits the same leakage.

F10 MEDIUM: Zero automated checks. `python -m unittest discover` reports 'Ran 0 tests ... OK'; no tests, CI, linter, type checker, or pre-commit config exists, which is why a script that cannot start and a metric returning 0.003 for a perfect ranking both reached a published commit.

F11 MEDIUM: Dependency posture. requirements.txt has only lower bounds, no hashes, no lockfile, no Python version — and behaviour is version-sensitive (whether ACT-18 parses determines the training set and the LSO split). pip-audit found exactly one advisory, PYSEC-2024-110 in scikit-learn 1.3.2 (TfidfVectorizer), which this pipeline never imports, so exposure is nil; it is reported only as evidence of the cost of unpinned requirements. No network, subprocess, eval/exec, pickle, or credential surface exists in the script.

findings: Manuscript access is now available: the readable DOCX and paragraph-numbered extraction supersede the original access limitation; biological claims, selected numerical claims, references and relevant tables were inspected.

Manuscript P641 says no in vivo models, but Qian 2024 reports TNBC xenograft growth suppression and four deaths among ten TH5427-treated mice after day 7; death causation and therapeutic window remain unresolved.

P700 Nguyen Science 2024 is bibliographically incorrect: the matching primary paper is Nguyen et al., Science 390(6778):1143–1150 (2025), DOI 10.1126/science.adv4257. Its noncatalytic PPAT claim is supported in its model context.

P701 Marques bioRxiv 2025 is a real but incomplete reference: DOI 10.1101/2025.03.16.643557, posted 17 March 2025. A relevant peer-reviewed 2026 Nature Communications report is DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-74489-9; degradation/protein loss can protect against 6-TG rather than simply improve anticancer action.
P206 confuses TH5427 biochemical IC50 (29 nM) with binding affinity; the 2.1 µM value is HL-60 ITDRF-CETSA apparent EC50, while DARTS concentrations are not fitted cellular EC50 values.
Balıkçı compound 9 differs from ibrutinib (1): it engages NUDT5/14, retains BTK engagement (EC50 0.377 ± 0.062 µM) and has BT-474 viability IC50 >10 µM. Target engagement is not anticancer efficacy.

ACT-02 TH1713 mono-Cl label conflicts with official deposited TH1713 identity. The ACT-01/pipeline reference differs from the deposited 1,3-dimethyl TH5427 representation. NC5-02 exactly duplicates training ACT-19 SMILES.

Manuscript reports 17 Page + 3 Balıkçı actives, but baseline source labels are 18 + 2; manuscript elsewhere states 28 actives/1400 decoys. The baseline repeats 26 unique decoy strings into 520 rows, contains no MTH1 proxy dataset and does not document the 18,412-compound screen.

Manuscript claims 30 permutations and p<.001, whereas code uses five and uncorrected exceedance fractions. Standard plus-one Monte Carlo resolution is 1/31=0.03225806451612903 for 30 draws, so the reported significance is not justified by that procedure.

Page hormone-dependent T47D evidence, Qian TNBC findings and later noncatalytic PPAT/thiopurine studies require context-specific synthesis, not a universal ATP, sanitation or catalytic-dependency mechanism.
limitations: No original PDF recovery, biological experiments, model/docking rerun, code changes, commits, PRs, deployments or remote-state modifications.
Readable manuscript reviewed for assigned biological-evidence scope, not all figures or author-policy declarations; converted table/unit/ligature artifacts require layout checks where flagged.

Wright 2016 and Qi 2022 full text was inaccessible through inspected endpoints; their evidence here is abstract-only. Individual manuscript Table 1 kinetic values were not independently source-verified.
No exhaustive systematic review, complete chemical graph/tautomer audit, complete raw/supplementary-data reanalysis or independent reproduction of primary-paper experiments.

recommended_fixes: Repair TH5427/TH1713 and analogue identity; attach original source compound numbers, exact structures, assay identifiers, endpoint types, units, thresholds, uncertainty and censoring to every label.

audits.unit: NUDT5 biology, inhibitor evidence and manuscript-reference audit
verified_facts: Exact audited baseline 8c2a1b6990df1e140e15ab5a0eabea69b70eee14 remains clean; five tracked files, 46 compounds (20 labelled active/26 decoys) and ten candidate rows.
DOCX ZIP integrity check passed; 720 body paragraphs, 13 Word tables, and 45,595 characters in supplied extraction. Tables 4/5/7 were checked directly in Word XML.

Eight primary full-text sources inspected for pertinent sections (Page, Pickup, Zhang, Balıkçı, Qian, Strefeler, Nguyen, Marques); Wright and Qi inspected as indexed abstracts; Marques 2025 preprint metadata/abstract independently verified.

The detailed Markdown report contains a 20-item literature/repository ledger, manuscript paragraph/table audit, assay-specific inhibitor comparison, high-level validation decision tree, source links and exact local-check scripts/outputs.
Both standard-library check scripts executed successfully and passed python -m py_compile; all changes are outside the repository.
Completed report uploaded for handoff; reference-definition, Markdown-fence and final clean-worktree checks passed.

findings: MANUSCRIPT ACCESS UPDATED: the readable DOCX and supplied P-numbered text were audited. The original PDF-unreadability limitation is superseded; the report cites manuscript paragraphs and tables alongside baseline code lines.

Methodological novelty is not demonstrated by the accessible evidence. The implemented equal-weight normalized mean belongs to an established consensus-scoring family; inspected prior work includes Charifson 1999, Ericksen 2017, CompScore 2019 and performance-derived fusion in Moshawih 2024. This is not exhaustive novelty clearance.

Important distinction: manuscript P277–P278 explicitly uses equal fusion weights of 0.25. Its claimed transfer mechanism is the separate alpha=0.3 MTH1 sample-weighted loss at P281–P294, not learned fusion weights. That loss and the 347 proxy compounds are absent from the pinned code/data.

Benchmark and deployment differ: pipeline.py L131–142/L216–220 min–max-normalizes pooled out-of-fold component arrays before averaging; L307–311 averages raw candidate components. Stored final-hit consensus values match manuscript Table 9 but are not reproduced by the displayed raw means or min–max averaging across those ten rows.

The five-fold benchmark has exact-negative leakage: each fold contains 104 held-out negative rows, all with identical training molecules. Independently, descriptor-only models strongly separate the unique molecules; neither result establishes NUDT5 activity prediction.

NC5-02 is canonically identical to labeled training active ACT-19, so it is not independent of the released training set. Under the manuscript's training-active similarity definition its AD is High, not Extrapolation; NC5-04 and NC5-06 also disagree with their stored tiers when evaluated against the 19 supplied valid actives.

The pinned BEDROC implementation fails a perfect-ordering check, returning approximately 0.00173 versus RDKit's approximately 1.000. The code runs five permutations, not thirty. Standard plus-one empirical permutation p-values cannot resolve p<0.001 from thirty permutations; minimum is 1/31.

Manuscript datasets/models/results conflict without an experiment mapping: 20 versus 28 actives, 520 versus 1,400 decoys, RF/GBT/RBF-SVM versus RF500/XGBoost/Tanimoto-SVM, and divergent Tables 5–7 metrics. The positional LSO split actually holds out only ACT-20 after parsing, not the claimed three actives.

The 18,412-compound library, 347 MTH1 proxies, docking/MM-GBSA/pharmacophore execution and 62% AD coverage remain unverified because their artifacts are absent. Candidate property/PAINS-filter code does exist and was not incorrectly treated as absent.

Reference correction: Nguyen T-A et al., A non-enzymatic role of Nudix hydrolase 5 in repressing purine de novo synthesis, is Science 2025, DOI 10.1126/science.adv4257—not 2024. Related Wu et al. DOI 10.1126/science.adx9717 is a distinct paper. Marques DOI 10.1101/2025.03.16.643557 was verified in full text and explicitly reports PROTACs; it does not establish ER-positive breast-cancer efficacy.

Dedicated disclosure sections were not found in the inspected text/XML. The report recommends author-confirmed funding, interests, contributions, affiliations, data/code availability and actual AI-use disclosures according to the chosen venue, without fabricating declarations or asserting misconduct.
limitations: Bounded inspected-literature assessment only: no systematic or exhaustive novelty search, patent clearance, priority certification or exhaustive subsequent-publication search.
The other nine candidates were not subjected to exact-structure commercial/public-database or patent novelty searches. Low similarity to TH5427 does not establish novelty.
Every training compound/IC50 was not independently mapped back to original assay records; CSV source labels and known chemical-series biology are not interchangeable with verified row-level activity.
Missing proxy, library and docking artifacts may exist elsewhere; their absence at this commit is an evidence gap, not proof that reported work never occurred.
DOCX access is resolved, but conversion artifacts remain in equations/ligatures/table layout. The unreadable original PDF was neither recovered nor used.

Diagnostic AUCs are descriptive, small-data, single-seed pooled OOF results with different split schemes for some models, not prospective estimates, formal AVE calculations or a fair algorithm superiority benchmark.
Some papers were inspected through official abstracts/metadata because full-text endpoints were unavailable; the report explicitly identifies access levels and source limitations.
Post-baseline Salimzhanov July 2026 and Agha September 2026 papers are separated as contemporary comparisons, not used to refute priority at the April 2026 commit.

No biological experiments, exhaustive permutation experiments, repository changes, further sessions, or public submissions were performed. No misconduct, affiliation, author declaration or publication outcome is inferred.
recommended_fixes: Reconstruct structure/assay provenance and unique target/proxy/negative inventories before modelling; log invalid records and distinguish presumed decoys from experimentally inactive compounds.

Prevent exact, analogue, scaffold and source leakage; document achieved property matching and evaluate broad chemical-series, scaffold/similarity-cluster, assay-source and time domains where feasible.

Separate proxy sample weighting, score fusion and AD estimation. Implement and ablate the proxy loss using alpha=0, 0.3, 1 and inner-tuned alpha, with explicit task/class normalization and no outer-test fitting.
Compare random/prevalence, six-descriptor, training-only nearest-neighbor, ECFP, individual component, raw/equal/rank and learned-fusion baselines on the same outer grouped splits.

Repair BEDROC and permutation calculations; report EF ceilings, top-k hit counts, AP/PR metrics, calibration and group-aware uncertainty. A significant permutation test cannot rule out property/source artifacts.

Freeze a common scoring transform for validation and candidates; publish full-precision component predictions and model artifacts; recompute AD against the declared training reference set and treat similarity bins as heuristic until calibrated.
Reconcile manuscript counts, algorithms, figures and Tables 4–7; distinguish proposed work from executed work; release or delimit library, proxy and docking artifacts and fix the input-path defect.

Use bounded current language: exploratory candidate-ranking prototype with an unvalidated proxy extension, not confirmed inhibitors, validated transfer learning or a demonstrated new consensus methodology.

Correct Nguyen's citation to 2025 and DOI 10.1126/science.adv4257; complete Marques's verified preprint citation while retaining its supported PROTAC description and avoiding therapeutic extrapolation.

If pursuing broad methodological claims, validate across independent target/proxy pairs and against established fusion methods. Biological claims require prospective biochemical/orthogonal/cellular evidence; none was generated in this audit.
audits.unit: Bounded TWCS novelty, manuscript reconciliation, and baseline/decoy-bias audit
verified_facts: Pinned repository HEAD remains 8c2a1b6990df1e140e15ab5a0eabea69b70eee14; final git status is clean. Only README.md, requirements.txt, compounds.csv, final_hits.csv and scripts/scripts/pipeline.py are tracked.

DOCX ZIP integrity passed; 720 body paragraphs and 13 Word tables were confirmed. Word table 13 contains the candidate SMILES table captioned Table 11. DOCX SHA-256: 11ef96824597f47daa1e6152caea8dc87cb3ebd6d78fd41be3baad14d31cca35.

New audit diagnostics on the unexpanded 45-molecule dataset: descriptor logistic-regression pooled OOF ROC-AUC 0.9939271255060729 under stratification and 0.9838056680161944 under scaffold grouping; scaffold-grouped ECFP4 RF AUC 0.9261133603238867; leave-one-Murcko-scaffold-out training-active maximum Tanimoto AUC 0.9210526315789473.

Active/decoy median MW values are 436.259/251.289 Da; median TPSA values are 126.87/47.72. Mean active-active, decoy-decoy and active-decoy Tanimoto values are approximately 0.5593, 0.1536 and 0.1115.
The replicated benchmark path gives rounded AUC 1.000 for RF, GBT, SVM and TWCS under the duplicated-negative split. This reproduces the magnitude, not a valid prospective conclusion.

At 20 actives/540 molecules and top-five retrieval, maximum EF1% is 27.0; the actual parsed 19/539 dataset has ceiling approximately 28.3684. The manuscript's blanket maximum-theoretical-100 comparison does not fit its stated dataset.

Five audit scripts, exact captured outputs, hashes and commands are included in the evidence archive and report. Final checks passed for script parsing, report structure, ZIP integrity, file hashes and unchanged baseline.

findings: MANUSCRIPT ACCESS UPDATE: the manuscript is now readable and HAS been audited. The prior unreadable-PDF limitation is superseded. DOCX SHA-256 11ef96824597f47daa1e6152caea8dc87cb3ebd6d78fd41be3baad14d31cca35, ZIP integrity check passed, independently re-parsed from word/document.xml: 720 top-level paragraphs, 1392 total paragraph nodes, 13 Word tables, 12 embedded media files.

BLOCKER 1 (arithmetic, not opinion): the claimed p < 0.001 is unobtainable from the stated design. With B=30 label permutations (P359) and the standard (r+1)/(B+1) estimator, the minimum attainable p-value is 1/31 = 0.0323, over 30x larger than the claimed p < 0.001 (P366). The naive r/B estimator gives 0, conventionally reported as p < 1/B = 0.033. Roughly B >= 1000 is needed. The repository hard-codes 5 permutations (1/6 = 0.167), not 30.

BLOCKER 2: the manuscript contradicts ITSELF on its own dataset sizes, independent of the repository. Actives: 20 (abstract P17-P26, results P327) vs 'Total: 28 unique NUDT5 actives' (P212) vs '28 actives from two scaffolds' twice in Limitations (P631, P650). Decoys: 520 (abstract, Table 4 caption P337) vs '50 per active (DUD-E), total 1,400 decoys' (P214) vs 26 in the repository.

BLOCKER 2b: Tables 4 and 7 report two irreconcilable metric sets for the same models. Table 4: RF BEDROC20 0.998, GBT 0.995, SVM 0.992, EF1% 27.0 for every method. Table 7: RF 0.41, XGBoost 0.38, SVM 0.44, EF1% 7.6-9.1. The text cites both as valid (P344-P347 vs P412-P413) without reconciling. LSO sensitivity is 0.33-0.67 (Table 5, abstract, conclusion P672) vs 0.38-0.63 (Table 7, Limitations P631). LOOCV is 0.90-0.95 (Table 6) vs 0.79-0.86 (Table 7) vs '>0.95' in prose (P377).

BLOCKER 3: zero author-policy disclosure statements anywhere in the document. Case-insensitive regex over all 1392 paragraph nodes including table cells returned 0 matches for funding, competing interests, author contributions, data availability, code availability, generative-AI/LLM use, ethics/IRB, and institutional affiliation. Notably there is NO code/data availability statement despite the repository existing. Authors are listed with two Gmail addresses and no affiliation (P4-P6). These are missing statements in an unsubmitted draft, not ethics violations, but every target venue requires several and AI use must be affirmatively stated rather than inferred as 'none'.

Model identity contradiction: Table 4 labels the SVM 'RBF kernel' while Methods (P232), Table 7 and the theory section (P184) all specify a Tanimoto kernel. The repository uses kernel='rbf', matching Table 4 and contradicting the stated method.

The 347 MTH1 proxy actives (P213) and the 18,412-compound library (P229) have no counterpart in any accessible tracked artifact; the repository reaches 520 decoys only by tiling its 26 decoys twenty times.

Citation defects (completeness/consistency, within publication scope): two unresolved drafting placeholders '[ref: Almansour 2023]' and '[ref: Frontiers 2020]' (P620-P621) support the manuscript's 'first study to...' novelty claim (P622), which a reviewer cannot evaluate against uncited prior work.

Reference [11] 'Nguyen, T.-A. et al. Science (2024)' (P700) is incomplete AND apparently mis-dated/mis-attributed. The cited PPAT claim (P93-P94) resolves to 'NUDT5 regulates purine metabolism and thiopurine sensitivity by interacting with PPAT', Science DOI 10.1126/science.adx9717, published November 2025, first author Zheng Wu, and the related 2025 bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.03.16.643506 (first author Jung-Ming G. Lin). Tuan-Anh Nguyen is a middle author on both and neither is dated 2024. The underlying science is real; the citation as written does not resolve to it.

Reference [12] 'Marques, A.-S.M.C. et al. bioRxiv (2025)' (P701) is substantively CORRECT but incomplete: resolves to 'Targeted Protein Degradation of NUDT5 Reveals an Unexpected Non-Enzymatic Role in 6-Thioguanine-Mediated Toxicity', bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.03.16.643557, posted 17 March 2025, first author Anne-Sophie M. C. Marques. First author and year correct; title and DOI missing; content matches its use for PROTAC degraders (P95).

Document structure defects: Table 9's score columns are corrupted/misaligned (duplicated values, orphaned AD tiers, NC5-01 Tanimoto appearing as both 0.88 and 0.53, contradicting Table 10 and the text at P439). Table 11 is captioned 'SMILES of all proposed NUDT5 candidate molecules' (P719) but contains bibliography entries; actual SMILES are in Table 13. Table 10 designates NC5-09 a 'covalent probe' while the manuscript states all candidates were designed for non-covalent interactions (P611-P612) with no covalent analysis anywhere.

Mitigating and genuinely creditable: the manuscript is unusually candid, conceding the classifiers 'effectively learn contains xanthine-oxadiazole substructure' (P600-P601), 'ML has near-zero power for novel scaffolds' (P650), 'all molecules are untested... any or all could be inactive' (P652-P653), and that outputs are 'computational hypotheses for chemical probe development, not drug candidates' (P644-P645). This materially lowers overclaiming risk but creates an internal inconsistency: the abstract and conclusion headline AUC = 1.000 / BEDROC20 = 0.999 (P670), a metric the authors elsewhere call uninformative.

The claimed methodological contribution is weaker than presented: TWCS 'in the equal-weight formulation used here (wk = 0.25)' reduces to the arithmetic mean of four scores by the manuscript's own statement (P277-P278), and the transfer weight alpha = 0.3 is asserted without sensitivity analysis (P291-P292).

Venue-policy conclusions unchanged: NeurIPS 2026 main-track deadlines have passed (abstract May 4, full paper May 6); Patterns journal-specific pages remain HTTP 403 access-limited so journal interpretations stay provisional atop fully inspected Elsevier parent policies; Nature flagship requires outstanding scientific importance not established by this record; Nature Portfolio is not synonymous with Nature.
limitations: The manuscript's 12 embedded figure images were NOT analyzed: figure pixel content, plotted ROC/BEDROC distributions and chemical-structure renderings remain unexamined, so figure/text consistency is unverified.

Reading the manuscript verifies what it claims, not whether those claims are true. No underlying dataset, docking run, fitted model or permutation test behind the reported numbers was obtained or regenerated.
No molecular parsing, docking, model fitting or biological experiment was executed; all manuscript findings are document-internal consistency checks, counts, exact arithmetic, and citation lookups.
Patterns journal-specific pages remained HTTP 403 access-limited; publisher-level Elsevier policies were fully inspected and are reported separately from provisional indexed journal excerpts.
Reference verification covered citation completeness and internal consistency as publication-policy defects; substantive biological adjudication of the cited literature belongs to the biology unit.

Some table structure and ligature loss stems from DOCX conversion; defects attributable to conversion were distinguished from defects re-confirmed in the source XML, but the final reference list should still be checked against the original document.

No acceptance probability, authorship/affiliation certification, ethics clearance, therapeutic claim or allegation of misconduct is supplied. Missing disclosure statements in an unsubmitted draft are not ethics violations.
recommended_fixes: Correct or withdraw the p < 0.001 claim: either raise the permutation count to roughly B >= 1000 and recompute, or report the attainable bound (p < 0.033 for B=30). This affects the abstract and conclusion and is arithmetic, not a matter of interpretation.

Resolve the 20-vs-28 actives and 520-vs-1,400-vs-26 decoy contradictions throughout, and supply immutable sources for the 347 MTH1 actives and the 18,412-compound library, or revise every dependent number including the cascade attrition table.
Reconcile Tables 4 vs 7 and Tables 5 vs 6 vs 7 so one metric set is authoritative, and state the SVM kernel consistently (Tanimoto per Methods or RBF per Table 4 and the code).

Add funding, competing-interest, author-contribution, data-availability, code-availability and AI-use statements plus institutional affiliations. Authors must supply these; do not infer 'none' from the document's silence, and point the data/code statement at the repository only once its contents match the manuscript.
Fix both '[ref: ...]' placeholders and complete references [11] and [12] with correct year, correct first author, title and DOI; mark [12] explicitly as a non-peer-reviewed preprint.
Repair Table 9's corrupted score columns and the Table 11/13 caption-content mismatch, and remove or substantiate the unsupported 'covalent probe' role for NC5-09.
Align the abstract with the paper's own self-critique by leading with leave-scaffold-out performance rather than within-series AUC = 1.000.
Demonstrate that TWCS is more than an arithmetic mean (weight sensitivity analysis, alpha ablation) before resting a methods-venue claim on it.
Narrow biological language to computational prioritization and testable hypotheses unless controlled biochemical, selectivity, cellular and mechanistic evidence is supplied.

No repository file was changed; no commit, push, PR, submission, external contact or child session was created. Only official public policy pages and two reference-resolution searches were queried externally.

findings: The accessible NUDT5 benchmark does not establish generalization to new inhibitors. Exact-negative leakage invalidates the original independent-evaluation interpretation; chemical identity, metric and provenance failures independently limit stronger claims.

Withdraw unsupported original generalization, BEDROC~0.999, p<0.001 from 5/30 permutations, ten-novel-independent-hit and demonstrated expanded-screening claims. Qualify computational prioritization, biological rationale, applicability domain, diversity and consensus-method contribution.

Parent headline should say highest observed AUROC among six prespecified methods in these three constructed evaluations, conditional on revised-run verification. Descriptor-only discrimination is consistent with physicochemical/source separation, not proof of its causal origin or generalizable NUDT5 prediction.

A corrected p=0.01 with 99 sampled permutations is a finite test floor under a specified null, not equal evidence strength across models or evidence against decoy/property/source confounding. The tested split/statistic must be stated; the supplied update did not identify it.

Cross-unit conflicts resolved: HBA differences are version-dependent, not universal CSV errors; Nguyen adv4257 is distinct from Wu adx9717; printed Table 11 is XML table 13; NC5-02 is a known tested published compound; nine stored consensus means exceed rounding tolerance.
DataPort metadata repetition is not independent validation. The accessible Zenodo archive contains only five baseline-matching files, not the expanded library, proxy or docking artifacts.
limitations: Parent-reported revised implementation, metrics and software checks were not independently inspected or rerun here. This is a baseline audit plus conditional headline adjudication.
Original unreadable PDF and DataPort subscription PDFs remain uninspected. Selected readable DOCX XML checks are not a complete manuscript or figure review.
Not every Page-labelled activity row was authenticated; expanded screening/proxy/docking/historical model artifacts are absent from the accessible baseline/archive.
No full historical model/docking rerun, biological experiment, exhaustive novelty/patent clearance, acceptance prediction or remote repository/public-record mutation was performed.
Some newer biology and venue-policy details have metadata/abstract or inherited-access limits, explicitly described in the report. No misconduct inference is made.
recommended_fixes: Preserve the original record; withdraw or explicitly label unsupported historical claims instead of silently replacing them with repaired diagnostics.
Authenticate row-level chemical/assay provenance, quarantine unresolved identities, and distinguish measured actives/inactives, unmeasured decoys, known controls and prospective candidates.
Use unique/group-aware evaluations, locked descriptor APIs/runtime, reference-tested metrics, training-only transformations, complete OOF predictions and a valid fully specified permutation null.
Independently audit an immutable revised code/data/environment/run manifest before treating parent-reported metrics or 40-test/lint/type/build/security outcomes as verified.
Keep descriptor-only success as a confounding warning, not a causal proof; require independent authenticated assay data to test predictive usefulness.
Require author approval for public metadata/declaration corrections and direct biochemical/cellular/selectivity evidence before inhibitor or therapeutic claims.
